bugs: Marking a task done with only `status` set leaves `completed_at` null, so the task is never counted in 'tasks completed in the last 7 days'. Nothing in Task sets `completed_at` when the status changes, and it is fillable for callers to set by hand. A probe confirmed this: update(['status'=>Done]) → count 0.
Membership changes do not clear the cache. There is no User observer, so adding or removing a team member leaves `members` wrong for up to 5 minutes (probe confirmed: 1 instead of 2).
The tests drive the dashboard through the `auth:sanctum` guard (`actingAs($user, 'sanctum')`). Bearer tokens are never exercised, even though a sanctum migration was added.
antipatterns: app/Services/TeamDashboard.php:53-58: version() does an extra Cache::add plus Cache::get on every request; versioned-key invalidation is heavier than `forget` and leaves orphaned entries behind.
app/Services/TeamDashboard.php:31-37: a hand-built whereIn subquery with `(clone $teamTasks)` instead of using a Team::tasks() hasManyThrough, which the code already defines.
app/Services/ExchangeRates.php:34,69: the lock wait (5) and the HTTP timeout (3) are hardcoded magic numbers; services.rates holds only the base_url.
app/Services/ExchangeRates.php:28 and :48: the `failing` check is duplicated both outside and inside the lock.
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:11-17: fakeRatesApi rebuilds the HTTP factory by hand (forgetInstance/clearResolvedInstance) to get around stub accumulation, which is ceremony.
tests/Feature/DashboardTest.php:104: a stray `$user->tokens()->count();` line that does nothing.
Neither dashboard path uses Cache::flexible, even though the brief explicitly allows serving stale data while it recomputes.
strengths: Versioned cache keys mean a slow recompute that started before a change cannot overwrite the fresh value (the comment at line 21 explains this).
The observers implement ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit and handle a task or project moving between teams using wasChanged/getPrevious.
The RatesUnavailable exception is renderable, which keeps the controller to one line.
The tests check the boundary of the 7-day window to the second, a 5-minute fallback for changes that bypass observers, and the 503 case when another request holds the lock and nothing is cached.
API routes live in a proper routes/api.php with Sanctum.

bugs: There is a small race on invalidation. A request that started recomputing before a commit can store its result after the afterCommit `forget` runs, leaving pre-change data cached for up to 5 minutes. The key is not versioned and nothing guards against this. It is rare and bounded.
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:4: `use Closure;` in the global namespace raises a PHP warning on every run (shown as warnings:1).
antipatterns: routes/web.php:11-14: the API endpoints sit in web.php under a `prefix('api')` group with session `auth`, instead of in routes/api.php.
app/Support/TeamDashboard.php:20: uses plain Cache::remember rather than Cache::flexible, even though the brief explicitly allows serving stale data for 5 minutes while it recomputes.
app/Observers/TaskObserver.php:14-15: always runs two queries on save, even when project_id did not change (no wasChanged guard).
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:175-182: the 'three second timeout' test only asserts the config value and never checks the timeout option sent with the request.
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:16-20: the switchable `$this->upstream` closure is a workaround for Http::fake stub accumulation.
strengths: A Task `saving` hook keeps completed_at consistent with status (stamped on Done, cleared on Open), so the 7-day count is correct however a task gets updated.
A UserObserver also clears the cache when members change; every observer clears both the old and new team via getOriginal.
TeamDashboard::forget is variadic and wraps the forgets in DB::afterCommit, written as clean collection code (`filter()->unique()->map(self::key(...))`).
It uses Team::tasks() hasManyThrough with the #[Scope] open/completedSince scopes, and `->map->only` as a higher-order message.
Rates logic: lock with block(), a double check after getting the lock, a 10-second failure cooldown, a last-known copy kept forever, and the timeout and lock wait in config.
Broad Pest tests: datasets of failure modes (timeout, 5xx, malformed body, empty rates), travel() for the TTLs, lock contention, and invalidation across teams.

v.rationale: Ranking: impl-2 first, impl-1 second. Both use the same overall design: a service class, invokable controllers, a FormRequest that upper-cases and validates the currency, model observers, and a lock with a last-known fallback. Neither uses Cache::flexible. Both suites pass (impl-2: 41 tests; impl-1: 29). I ran probe tests against both and then deleted them. impl-2 passed every probe, including invalidation inside a transaction, deleting a project, and the timeout option actually being 3. impl-1 failed two: marking a task done without setting completed_at drops it from the 7-day count, because nothing in impl-1 sets completed_at; and member changes are not reflected until the cache expires. impl-1's versioned keys are more robust against the recompute race, but they add a cache write on every request and more ceremony. Its rates service also hardcodes the timeout and lock wait, and its test helpers are clumsier. impl-2's weaknesses are smaller: API routes in web.php, a rare race on invalidation, a warning-producing `use Closure;`, and a timeout test that only checks config.
